To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the asymptotic statistics of determinantal processes can be described as the superposition (in the sense of stochastic processes) of a Gaussian noise and an (independent) Poisson point process.

the correlation functions of a determinantal point process with random matrix statistics at small scale and Poisson statistics at large scale can be described in terms of a superposition of a correlated Gaussian noise and a Poisson process.

(1) the asymptotic behavior of the cumulant generating function of the linear statistics is determined by the asymptotic behavior (in the bulk or on the edge) of the correlation kernel, and (2) the asymptotic of the correlation kernel depends on the asymptotics of a certain determinant.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a determinantal process is a random point process with a correlation kernel.

, for any linear statistic, the process converges in law to a random variable which is the sum of a Gaussian and a Poisson random variable, with the Gaussian part having an explicit variance and a correlation kernel depending on the expected percolation configuration.
, in the limit, the process is a mixture of two Poisson processes, with a correlation kernel that is the superposition of the kernel of the determinantal process and of a Gaussian noise kernel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Poisson statistics of the Bernoulli deleted determinantal point process is a universal feature of the process and is independent of the potential and the number of particles.
we have shown that the Poisson statistics of a determinantal process can be recovered by removing the appropriate number of particles in a log-gas.

, in the presence of a percolation on a determinantal process, the correlation structure of the point process is not affected at small scales, but the variance of any local statistic is renormalized by an independent Poisson noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the universality class of a determinantal process can be changed by a simple Bernoulli percutation, without changing the underlying determinantal structure.
the universal behavior of linear statistics in random matrix theory can be recovered in the presence of a large number of random holes, as long as the holes are not too close to each other.
the crossover between Poisson and random matrix statistics is not a phase transition but a smooth crossover.
